# double-meh-bundler — full reference

> Server side of the double-meh bundle protocol. One bundled request in (many GETs as one PUT), one enveloped response out — or, when the client negotiates `…bundle+jsonl`, a stream of parts flushed as their upstreams complete. Web-standard fetch-handler core; dependency-free duck-typed adapters. Zero runtime dependencies. ESM-only. Node >= 18 (code floor: web-standard `fetch`/`Request`/`Response` globals), Bun, Deno; the core runs anywhere a fetch handler does (service workers, edge runtimes).

## Why bundle

- Compression locality: many small JSON responses share one compression window (~40–48% fewer bytes measured on bursts of small responses; ~16–22% on medium).
- Cross-origin aggregation: one bundler origin fans out to any backend service — HTTP/2 multiplexing is per-origin and cannot do this.
- h1 paths: over HTTP/1.1 (still the norm for origins behind no edge) bundling also recovers the connection-cap win.

The client (double-meh's `io.bundle`) keeps per-request semantics intact: per-URL caching, ETag/304 revalidation, retry, and error granularity all survive bundling.

## Module: double-meh-bundler (src/index.js)

Platform-pure — no `node:` imports; runs in service workers and edge runtimes unchanged.

### createBundler(options) → (request: Request) => Promise<Response>

Options (`BundlerOptions`):

- `isUrlAcceptable: (url: string, request: Request) => boolean` — REQUIRED, no default; the constructor throws a TypeError without it. The allow-list is the security boundary: a part with an unacceptable URL becomes a synthetic 403 part, the bundle proceeds.
- `resolveUrl?: (url: string) => string` — maps public part URLs to internal ones (e.g. `/api/x` → `http://api.internal:8080/api/x`). Default: identity. The result resolves against the bundler request's own URL, so relative outputs work.
- `fetch?: (request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>` — the upstream fetch. Default `globalThis.fetch`. Inject for tests, mocks, or in-process serving.
- `maxRequests?: number` — hard cap on parts per bundle; above it the whole request is refused with 400 problem+json. Default 20.
- `partTimeout?: number` — per-part upstream timeout (ms). Implemented as an explicit race (works even when the injected upstream ignores AbortSignals); a timed-out part becomes a synthetic 504 part. Default 10000.
- `streaming?: boolean` — serve `application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+jsonl` when the request's `Accept` names it exactly. Default true, but entirely client-driven: a client that never asks never gets it. Forced off whenever `processBundle` is configured.
- `onBundleStart?: (context: {request, parts}) => unknown` — observer, fired once after the protocol guards pass and before the fan-out; `parts` are the request-side descriptors.
- `onItemFinish?: (part, context) => unknown` — observer, fired per part once it reaches its final shape (after `processResult`). Context: `{request, requestPart, durationMs}` where `durationMs` is upstream fetch time excluding the transform.
- `onBundleFinish?: (bundle, context) => unknown` — observer, fired once when the envelope reaches its final shape (after `processBundle`), before serialization. Context: `{request, durationMs}` where `durationMs` is the whole bundle, from the guards passing to the finished envelope.
- `processResult?: (part, context) => part | null | undefined | Promise<…>` — transform one finished part; awaited. Same context as `onItemFinish`.
- `processBundle?: (bundle, context: {request}) => bundle | null | undefined | Promise<…>` — transform the whole `{v: 1, parts}` envelope after the sort and before serialization; awaited.

Hook contract:

- Observers (`onBundleStart`, `onItemFinish`, `onBundleFinish`) are **not awaited** and their throws/rejections are swallowed: instrumentation never changes behavior, so a broken metrics counter cannot fail a bundle. A slow observer never delays the response.
- Observer order per bundle: `onBundleStart`, then one `onItemFinish` per part (fan-out order, not request order), then `onBundleFinish`. `onBundleStart` fires only after the protocol guards pass, and `onBundleFinish` only when an envelope was actually produced — a start with no matching finish means `processBundle` threw.
- Transforms (`processResult`, `processBundle`) are awaited. A **nullish return keeps the original** value — a dropped part would leave the client's waiter unresolved, so the forgiving contract is deliberate.
- A throwing `processResult` makes that part a synthetic 500 (id preserved, so the client's waiter still resolves) while siblings ship normally; a throwing `processBundle` has no per-part isolation left and fails the bundle with a 500 problem+json whose title carries no consumer message.
- `processResult` runs **before** the base64 sort, so a transform that turns a part binary still sorts last and keeps the compression-window locality; `processBundle` runs after it and owns whatever ordering it produces.
- Every hook is validated at construction: a supplied non-function throws a TypeError naming the option (a mistyped hook name would otherwise be silently inert).

Handler behavior:

- Methods: PUT and POST accepted; anything else → 405 with `Allow: PUT, POST`.
- Body must parse as JSON with `{v: 1, parts: []}` — otherwise 400 problem+json (`malformed bundle request body` / `not a v1 bundle request`).
- Empty `parts` → valid no-op: `{v: 1, parts: []}`.
- Sub-requests: GET only (non-GET parts → synthetic 405 part); headers from the part's whitelist (`accept`, `accept-language`, `if-none-match`, `if-modified-since`, case-insensitive) plus `authorization`/`cookie` propagated from the outer request; `redirect: 'follow'`.
- Parts echo their request `url` (the client's cache identity), never the redirected final URL.
- Part response headers ride minus wire-form/hop-by-hop/cookie-setting ones (`content-encoding`, `content-length`, `connection`, `keep-alive`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`, `te`, `trailer`, `set-cookie`).
- Part bodies: JSON content types ride inline (parsed); `text/*` as strings; anything else as base64 with `encoding: "base64"`; 204/304 parts carry no body. Binary (base64) parts sort last — stable sort — so text parts stay contiguous in one compression window.
- Failures are per part, never per bundle: allow-list refusal → synthetic 403; unresolvable URL → synthetic 400; upstream throw → synthetic 502 (with the message); timeout → synthetic 504; upstream declared JSON but unparseable → synthetic 502.
- The envelope: `Content-Type: application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+json`, `Cache-Control: no-store` (parts carry their own cache headers; the envelope must never be cached as a unit).

### Constants

- `REQUEST_MIME` = `application/vnd.double-meh.bundle-request+json`
- `BUNDLE_MIME` = `application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+json`

## Module: double-meh-bundler/node.js

### toNodeHandler(handler, options?) → (req, res, next?) => Promise<void>

Duck-typed `(IncomingMessage, ServerResponse, next?)` — covers bare `node:http` and Express (Express req/res are supersets; no framework import exists in the module). Options (`NodeHandlerOptions`):

- `compress?: boolean` — gzip the envelope when the client's `Accept-Encoding` allows; default true (bare node has no compression middleware idiom, and compression is the bundle's payoff).

Errors: forwarded to `next(error)` when a `next` function is supplied (Express style); otherwise a 500 `application/problem+json` is sent.

```js
import {createServer} from 'node:http';
import {createBundler} from 'double-meh-bundler';
import {toNodeHandler} from 'double-meh-bundler/node.js';

const bundle = toNodeHandler(
  createBundler({
    isUrlAcceptable: url => url.startsWith('/api/'),
    resolveUrl: url => new URL(url, 'http://api.internal:8080').href
  })
);
createServer((req, res) => (req.url.startsWith('/bundle') ? bundle(req, res) : notFound(res))).listen(3000);
```

## Module: double-meh-bundler/koa.js

### toKoaMiddleware(handler) → (ctx) => Promise<void>

Duck-typed against a structural `KoaLikeContext` (deliberately not `@types/koa`): `req`, `href`, `method`, `status`, `body`, `set(field, value)` — the real Koa `Context` satisfies it. Terminal middleware — never calls `next`; mount it on the bundle route. Compression is middleware business: put `koa-compress` in front.

Implementation note: Koa's body setter forces status 204 when assigned `null` — the adapter uses an empty string for bodyless responses so real statuses (e.g. the 405 method guard) survive.

```js
import Koa from 'koa';
import route from 'koa-route';
import {createBundler} from 'double-meh-bundler';
import {toKoaMiddleware} from 'double-meh-bundler/koa.js';

const app = new Koa();
app.use(route.put('/bundle', toKoaMiddleware(createBundler({isUrlAcceptable}))));
```

Streamed responses (`application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+jsonl`):

- Negotiated by the client naming the type in `Accept`; matching is an exact essence comparison per entry, because `BUNDLE_MIME` is a string prefix of `BUNDLE_JSONL_MIME` and a `startsWith` test would confuse them. Exported as `BUNDLE_JSONL_MIME`.
- Framing: line 1 is the envelope header `{"v":1}`; every later line is exactly one part in the unchanged v1 part shape. `v` stays 1 — the framing changed, not the parts — and the content type is what distinguishes the two forms.
- Parts are written as their upstreams complete, so they arrive in completion order rather than request order; correlation is by `id`, which the format has always required. Base64 parts are still held to the end of the stream (text-first locality outranks early binary delivery).
- Protocol guards (405, 400) answer before any stream opens, so an error is always a normal buffered `problem+json` response.
- Hooks: `processResult` applies before a part is written; `onItemFinish` fires per written part; `onBundleFinish` fires after the last line with the parts in shipped order. `processBundle` cannot apply to a stream and therefore disables streaming rather than being skipped — a configured transform may be redacting, so silently dropping it would be worse than not streaming.
- A part that cannot be serialized (a `processResult` returning something with a cycle) becomes a synthetic 500 line rather than breaking the stream.
- Compression: per-part flushing is required for parts to actually arrive early, and costs +25% bytes at 10 parts / +57% at 50 versus one-shot gzip of the buffered envelope. The node adapter switches to `Z_SYNC_FLUSH` automatically for `+jsonl` responses; Koa users must pass `{gzip: {flush: constants.Z_SYNC_FLUSH}}` to `koa-compress`.

## Wire format v1 (normative summary)

Request (`application/vnd.double-meh.bundle-request+json`):

```json
{"v": 1, "parts": [{"id": "a", "url": "/api/users/42", "method": "GET", "headers": {"accept": "application/json", "if-none-match": "\"v7\""}}]}
```

Response (`application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+json`):

```json
{"v": 1, "parts": [
  {"id": "a", "url": "/api/users/42", "status": 200, "headers": {"content-type": "application/json", "etag": "\"v8\"", "vary": "Accept"}, "body": {"name": "…"}},
  {"id": "b", "url": "/api/roles", "status": 304, "headers": {"etag": "\"v3\""}},
  {"id": "c", "url": "/api/broken", "status": 502, "synthetic": true, "headers": {"content-type": "text/plain"}, "body": "connection refused"}
]}
```

Rules: correlation by client-assigned `id` (never order); parts always echo `url` (+ optional `accept`) so unclaimed parts can seed client caches; `synthetic: true` means the transport to the upstream never happened (client maps it to a transport error), while a genuine upstream non-2xx part keeps its status and body (client maps it to its normal HTTP-error path); base64 parts last; the envelope is `no-store`.

## Errors

- 405 + `Allow: PUT, POST` — wrong method on the bundler endpoint.
- 400 `application/problem+json` — malformed body, unknown version, too many parts.
- Per-part synthetic statuses: 400 (no/unresolvable url), 403 (allow-list), 405 (non-GET), 502 (upstream failure/bad JSON), 504 (timeout).
